screening.reason: Reports a resting-state functional-connectivity group-difference (mega-)analysis between autism and neurotypical participants using ABIDE I and ABIDE II alongside EU-AIMS LEAP (Inclusion 2, 3)

evidence_spans.text:
The study 
included resting-state fMRI and clinical data from the LEAP and the ABIDE I and II initiatives, 
of 1824 (796 with autism) participants with age range 5-58 years.
evidence_spans.claim: Mega-analysis combines EU-AIMS LEAP with ABIDE I and ABIDE II for a total of 1824 participants (796 autism).

evidence_spans.claim: Table 1 breaks the combined sample down by dataset: ABIDE I contributed 369 autism/481 NT, and ABIDE II contributed 205 autism/347 NT.

evidence_spans.text:
Resting-state fMRI and structural scans were obtained using 3T MRI scanners at 32 scanning 
sites (Supplement Section 3).
evidence_spans.claim: Data were acquired at 32 scanning sites across the combined datasets.

evidence_spans.text:
ComBat (36) was used to remove the confounding 
effects of scanning site from the fMRI data (Supplement Section 4).
evidence_spans.claim: Site effects were harmonised using ComBat.

evidence_spans.text:
To 
assess FC group differences, a general linear model was fitted to each edge, including 
diagnosis, age, sex, and mean framewise displacement (FD) as covariates.
evidence_spans.claim: Group differences were assessed with a GLM per edge including diagnosis, age, sex and mean FD as covariates, analysed with the Network Based Statistic.

evidence_spans.text:
At the primary component-forming threshold of p<0.05, the NT>ASD contrast revealed 
hypoconnectivity in autism that encompassed 13,001 edges (17.1% of the total number of 
edges) linking 376 brain regions (pfwe<0.001; Figure 1A-C). The ASD>NT contrast revealed 
hyperconnectivity in autism, including 16,767 edges (22% of the total number of edges; 
pfwe<0.001) and linking all 390 brain regions
evidence_spans.claim: Autism showed both brain-wide hypoconnectivity (13,001 edges, 17.1%) and hyperconnectivity (16,767 edges, 22%) relative to neurotypicals, each significant after family-wise error correction.

evidence_spans.text:
To further demonstrate the robustness and replicability of our findings we conducted the full 
FC mapping and analysis of group differences separately in the LEAP and 
ABIDE 1&2 data.
evidence_spans.claim: Findings were replicated by repeating the full analysis separately within LEAP and within the combined ABIDE I/II data.

assessments.support: Paper states "Details about our exclusion criteria are provided in Supplement Section 2" but the exclusion rules themselves are not given in the body text.
N by diagnosis and dataset (ABIDE I 369/481, ABIDE II 205/347), age range, sex and site count (32 sites) reported in Table 1 and text.

Preprocessing pipeline name/version not stated in the body text; only Schaefer-400 + Harvard-Oxford subcortical parcellation and ComBat harmonisation are named, with pipeline detail deferred to an unavailable supplement.

"Each site within ABIDE followed their individual diagnostic procedures for establishing an autism diagnosis, although the majority of the sites used the Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule (35) and/or Autism Diagnostic Interview-Revised (32)."
GLM included diagnosis, age, sex and mean FD as covariates; ComBat used for site.
Site harmonised with ComBat; age/sex/motion included as covariates; sensitivity analyses for IQ, sex, medication and ADHD comorbidity reported.
Pearson correlation FC matrices from Schaefer-400 + Harvard-Oxford subcortical ROIs, Gaussian-gamma mixture normalised.
Network Based Statistic with family-wise error-corrected threshold (pfwe<.001) across primary component thresholds.

risk_of_bias.summary: Large multi-dataset mega-analysis with clearly reported N by dataset/diagnosis, diagnosis source, covariate handling (age, sex, mean FD, ComBat site harmonisation) and FWE-corrected network-based statistics; main gap is that the preprocessing pipeline name/version and the exact exclusion rules are deferred to a supplement not present in the extracted text.

charting.title: Connectome-wide Mega-analysis Reveals Robust Patterns of Atypical Functional Connectivity in Autism
charting.diagnosis_assessment: Clinical diagnosis per site; majority used ADOS and/or ADI-R
charting.n_disordered: 574 (ABIDE I 369 + ABIDE II 205); combined with EU-AIMS LEAP for a total autism N of 796
charting.healthy_status_confirmed: Neurotypical controls reported no psychiatric diagnosis
charting.n_controls: 828 (ABIDE I 481 + ABIDE II 347); combined with EU-AIMS LEAP for a total NT N of 1028
charting.specific_features: Pearson-correlation connectome; Schaefer 400-region cortical parcellation + 15 Harvard-Oxford subcortical ROIs (390 regions, 75,855 edges)
charting.feature_extraction_tools: ComBat (site harmonisation); pipeline name/version not reported in available text
charting.feature_change_direction: Hypoconnectivity in sensory/somatomotor and higher-order attentional networks; hyperconnectivity involving the default mode network, subcortex (thalamus, striatum), and cognitive control network
charting.specific_algorithms: Network Based Statistic (NBS); canonical correlation analysis (CCA) for brain-behaviour associations
charting.validation_methodology: Split-sample replication: full analysis repeated separately in LEAP and in combined ABIDE I/II data
charting.summary_key_findings: Autism is associated with a brain-wide pattern of both hypoconnectivity (13,001 edges, 17.1% of all edges, pfwe<0.001) and hyperconnectivity (16,767 edges, 22% of all edges, pfwe<0.001) relative to neurotypicals; findings replicated separately in the ABIDE I/II subsample and in LEAP, and were associated with clinical symptom dimensions via CCA.
charting.features_associated_disorder: Hypoconnectivity: visual-somatomotor, within-somatomotor, somatomotor-dorsal attention, somatomotor-salience, amygdala-somatomotor/visual. Hyperconnectivity: DMN-cognitive control network, thalamus and medial temporal areas with striatum/thalamus.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Group-difference (associational) mega-analysis; ABIDE I (369 autism/481 NT) and ABIDE II (205 autism/347 NT) combined with EU-AIMS LEAP (222/200) for a total of 796 autism/1028 NT across 32 sites
narrative_row.methods: Pearson-correlation connectomes from Schaefer-400 cortical + 15 Harvard-Oxford subcortical ROIs; ComBat site harmonisation; per-edge GLM with diagnosis, age, sex, mean FD covariates assessed with the Network-Based Statistic at FWE-corrected thresholds; canonical correlation analysis linking connectivity to clinical symptom dimensions.
narrative_row.outcomes: Autism showed brain-wide hypoconnectivity (13,001 edges, 17.1% of edges, pfwe<0.001), concentrated in sensory/somatomotor/attention networks, and hyperconnectivity (16,767 edges, 22% of edges, pfwe<0.001), concentrated in DMN/subcortical connections; pattern replicated separately in LEAP and in combined ABIDE I/II data.
narrative_row.key_limitations: Preprocessing pipeline name/version and exact exclusion criteria are deferred to a supplement not present in the extracted full text; analysis excluded the cerebellum due to poor scan coverage; most participants under 25 years old; sex ratio imbalanced between groups.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: A large multi-site mega-analysis explicitly reporting ABIDE I and ABIDE II subsample sizes separately and replicating its connectome-wide findings within the combined ABIDE I/II data alone.
